drug_class: Intravenous Nutritional Supplement / Lipid Injectable Emulsion
purpose: Fat emulsions are given through an IV to provide your body with calories, healthy fats, and essential fatty acids when you are unable to eat on your own or get enough nutrition through regular food. They are often used in hospitals for patients recovering from surgery, serious illness, or conditions that prevent normal eating. They are a key part of what doctors call 'total parenteral nutrition' or TPN, which is a way of feeding your body completely through your veins.
how_it_works: These are tiny droplets of fat mixed with water in a way that your body can safely use through an IV line. Once in your bloodstream, your body breaks down these fat droplets just like it would digest fats from food, using them for energy and to support cell function. They also provide essential fatty acids that your body cannot make on its own, which are needed to keep your organs, skin, and immune system healthy.
common_side_effects: Some patients may notice a mild fever, chills, or a flushing sensation during the infusion. You might experience nausea, a headache, or a feeling of fullness. Some people notice a temporary change in the color of their blood work results, which is normal and goes away. Mild pain or irritation at the IV site can also occur.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have a severe allergy to eggs, soybeans, peanuts, or fish, as some fat emulsions contain these ingredients. If you have liver disease, pancreatitis, or very high triglyceride (blood fat) levels, your doctor needs to know before starting this treatment. Rarely, serious reactions like difficulty breathing, chest pain, or signs of fat buildup in the blood can occur, so medical staff will monitor you closely. This medication should only be given in a medical setting where you can be watched carefully.
typical_dosing: The dose is carefully calculated by your medical team based on your weight, age, medical condition, and how much nutrition your body needs. It is given slowly through an IV, usually over 12 to 24 hours. Your healthcare team will regularly check your blood to make sure your body is handling the fat properly and adjust the dose if needed. You will not manage this medication at home on your own without close medical supervision.
